definition: Indexed grammars are a generalization of context-free grammars in that nonterminals are equipped with lists of flags, or index symbols.
details: The language produced by an indexed grammar is called an indexed language.
story: Picture an engineer at a cluttered workbench, turning a clever idea over in their hands until it finally clicks. At its heart it is a simple notion, once you strip away the fancy name. A small key that opens a much bigger door. It is one of those ideas that feels obvious only after someone shows it to you. And that idea, made concrete, is Indexed grammar.
